source_paths=['spectrometer_x_ray_crystal/channel/profiles_line_integrated/velocity_tor']; documentation='This quantity is the effective toroidal bulk-flow velocity of plasma averaged along a diagnostic line of sight. It represents motion around the machine axis rather than a local velocity at one point or an accumulated line signal.

For a line of sight with path length $L$, the line-averaged toroidal velocity is defined by

$$
\overline{v}_{\phi} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} v_{\phi}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\ell$ is distance along the line of sight, $L$ is its total path length, and $v_{\phi}(\ell)=\mathbf{v}(\ell)\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the local toroidal component of the plasma bulk velocity. The normalization by $L$ distinguishes this velocity from a line-integrated quantity. The generic plasma designation does not select a particular ion species or charge state, unlike species-resolved quantities such as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.'

The extent is defined by the separation of the two boundary coordinates along $X_2$:

$$
H_2 = X_{2,\max} - X_{2,\min}
$$

where $X_{2,\max}$ and $X_{2,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum aperture-boundary coordinates along $X_2$, and $H_2$ is the resulting length.

This quantity describes the second local tangential dimension and is distinct from the [width of the neutron detector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_diagnostic_aperture), which measures the corresponding first local tangential dimension. source_paths=['edge_transport/model/ggd/ion/momentum/v/z']; documentation='The vertical ion momentum convection velocity is the vertical effective velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species. The vertical direction is the $Z$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the vertical label names the velocity direction, not the transported momentum component. Because this is an intensive species-level quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of that species.

The vertical convective flux density of an ion-momentum component is represented by:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z} = p_{i,a}\,V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}
$$

where $p_{i,a}=n_i m_i u_{i,a}$ is the ion momentum density associated with ion flow component $u_{i,a}$, $n_i$ is the ion density, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $a$ labels the momentum component being transported, $V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}$ is the vertical ion momentum convection velocity, and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z}$ is the corresponding vertical convective flux density of that momentum component.

This quantity is the convective coefficient multiplying local ion momentum density; it excludes diffusive viscosity, residual stress, and explicit momentum sources. It is not generally identical to the bulk [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity), because it characterizes transport of momentum density rather than the mean particle flow. The unprojected coefficient is [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity); other projections specify their own directions.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection carries the selected ion momentum density toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.'
